title: Storage Accounts: Redundancy, Replication and Encryption

header.html: Create and configure storage accounts; configure Azure Storage redundancy; configure object replication; configure storage account encryption; manage data by using Azure Storage Explorer and AzCopy
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1The storage account

An Azure storage account is a namespace (a unique name, <name>.blob.core.windows.net) that holds your storage services.

Service Holds
Blob Objects (files, images, backups)
Files File shares (SMB, NFS)
Queue Messages between application components
Table NoSQL key-attribute data
Account type (performance) Use
Standard general-purpose v2 Default for most uses (all services)
Premium block blobs Low latency for blobs
Premium file shares High-performance file shares
Premium page blobs VM disks (unmanaged) and page blobs

The account name must be globally unique (3 to 24 lowercase letters and numbers). Region, performance and redundancy are chosen at creation.

2Redundancy

Option Copies and location Protects against
LRS (locally redundant) 3 copies in one datacenter Disk or rack failure
ZRS (zone-redundant) 3 copies across 3 availability zones in the region A datacenter (zone) failure
GRS (geo-redundant) LRS in the primary region + asynchronous copy (LRS) to a secondary region A regional outage
GZRS (geo-zone-redundant) ZRS in the primary + LRS in the secondary region Zone and regional failure
RA-GRS / RA-GZRS As GRS / GZRS, plus read access to the secondary endpoint Regional outage with read availability
Exam tip

. Zone failure only = ZRS. Region failure = GRS or GZRS. Need to read from the secondary region = RA-GRS or RA-GZRS. Secondary data is replicated asynchronously, so a failover can lose recent writes.

You can change redundancy after creation (some conversions need a migration request). [Verify live]

3Object replication

Object replication asynchronously copies block blobs from a source container to a destination container, in another account or region, according to rules (with optional prefix filters).

Requirement Fact
Prerequisites Blob versioning enabled on both accounts, change feed on the source
Direction One-way per rule (source to destination)
Use Lower latency for readers in another region, data distribution, compliance copies

4Encryption

Topic Fact
At rest Always on: all data is encrypted with 256-bit AES; cannot be turned off
Keys Microsoft-managed keys (default) or customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault (or Managed HSM)
Infrastructure encryption Optional second layer of encryption
In transit Secure transfer required forces HTTPS (and SMB encryption for Files); set the minimum TLS version
Exam tip

. "Control the encryption keys" = customer-managed keys in Key Vault.

5Storage Explorer and AzCopy

Tool Use
Azure Storage Explorer GUI app to browse and manage blobs, files, queues and tables
AzCopy Command-line tool to copy and sync data quickly: azcopy login, azcopy copy, azcopy sync; authenticate with Entra ID or a SAS token
Exam tip

. Storage encryption at rest cannot be turned off; the question is only who holds the keys (Microsoft or you in Key Vault).

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1An application must keep data available if one datacenter in the region fails, with the lowest cost that meets this. Which option fits?

  • AZRS
  • BLRS
  • CGRS
  • DRA-GZRS
Show the answer

Answer: A. ZRS spreads copies across availability zones in the region.

S2A company needs to read data from the secondary region during a regional outage. Which option fits?

  • ALRS
  • BZRS
  • CRA-GRS
  • DGRS
Show the answer

Answer: C. Read-access variants allow reads from the secondary endpoint.

S3A team wants to copy new blobs automatically to a storage account in another region. What should be configured?

  • AA resource lock
  • BA budget
  • CObject replication
  • DA snapshot
Show the answer

Answer: C. Object replication copies block blobs between accounts asynchronously.

S4Which prerequisites does object replication need?

  • ABlob versioning, and change feed on the source
  • BA Premium account in the same region as the source account
  • CArchive tier on all blobs in the source container
  • DA static website enabled on both storage accounts
Show the answer

Answer: A. Versioning on both accounts and change feed on the source are required.

S5A team wants control of the keys that encrypt a storage account. What should it use?

  • ATurn encryption off and rely on the network firewall
  • BPublic access with the account key kept in the application
  • CCustomer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault
  • DA snapshot of the account that is encrypted by Microsoft
Show the answer

Answer: C. Customer-managed keys give control over the encryption keys.

S6An administrator needs to copy 2 TB of blobs between accounts from the command line. Which tool fits?

  • AAzCopy
  • BAzure Advisor
  • CAzure Policy
  • DNetwork Watcher
Show the answer

Answer: A. AzCopy copies and syncs large data sets.

6.2 Recall questions

R1How many copies does LRS keep, and where?

Show the answer

Three, in one datacenter.

R2What does ZRS protect against?

Show the answer

The failure of one availability zone (datacenter).

R3What does RA in RA-GRS add?

Show the answer

Read access to the secondary region.

R4Can storage encryption at rest be turned off?

Show the answer

No, it is always on.

R5Name the four storage services.

Show the answer

Blob, Files, Queue and Table.

R6What does secure transfer required enforce?

Show the answer

HTTPS for requests to the account.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Services Blob, Files, Queue, Table; general-purpose v2 is the default
Redundancy LRS (datacenter), ZRS (zones), GRS (region), GZRS (zones + region), RA- for read access
Object replication async block blobs; versioning + change feed
Encryption always on at rest; customer-managed keys in Key Vault; secure transfer
Tools Storage Explorer (GUI), AzCopy (command line)
